claims.natural_statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 247 (An infinite finitely presented residually finite 2-group and a finitely presented nil algebra.; papers: An infinite finitely presented residually finite 2-group; An infinite finitely presented periodic group; Lean status: Partially/Comparator formalized (lean/docs/247.md)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.

For all legal sufficiently large hierarchy parameters, clean encoding preserves nonzero upper words under arbitrary replacements, and every consecutive-cut interval of a nonzero word normalizes by replacements supported inside the interval.

Lemma fr:context: from complete clean blocks all elementary replacements preserve structural, transaction and checker syntax; distinct transactions do not own cells of the same block, including at abutting boundaries.

Lemma fr:verification: on a complete fixed-payload transaction region, arbitrary bidirectional full-head paths from A_1 with zero registers reach success exactly when every addressed clause is true, and cannot reach format, nonblank-register, or false-after-gate zeros.

The complete-full-head assertion of fr:rollback holds for arbitrary forged phases and registers. A boundary-cursor region containing its known first position and its entire acquired prefix can be released inside that prefix.

For every legal sufficiently large parameter h, the actual clause address formulas and fixed program accept exactly the elementary next-parameter rule entries, with the displayed input, clause and certificate bounds.
Lemma fr:faithful: E_h simulates every next-parameter elementary relation and zero, and no replacement sequence from E_h(w) for nonzero upper word w reaches a lower elementary zero.

Lemma fr:token-normalization: every interval between consecutive cuts of a nonzero word contains one to k complete blocks and has an isolated canonical normalization, including arbitrary forged full-head states.
A boundary-cursor region can always be released inside its acquired interval.

In the explicitly enlarged projection of the unary-source and zero schemas in Main.lean, for all natural q>=3 and 1<p<q, a format-valid singleton B cursor at C(p) is nonzero and cannot reach an all-idle word.
claims.formal_statement:
import Mathlib

namespace FiniteRuleBoundary

inductive Structural where
  | core : Nat → Structural
  | palette : Nat → Structural
  | stop : Structural
  deriving DecidableEq

inductive Marker where
  | idle | left | boundary | full | right
  deriving DecidableEq

structure Cell where
  structural : Structural
  marker : Marker
  formatOK : Bool
  checkerIdle : Bool
  deriving DecidableEq

def cursor (p : Nat) : Cell :=
  ⟨.core p, .boundary, true, true⟩

inductive Unary : Cell → Cell → Prop where
  | create (a b : Cell) :
      a.structural = .core 1 → b.structural = .core 1 →
      a.marker = .idle → b.marker = .boundary → Unary a b
  | uncreate (a b : Cell) :
      a.structural = .core 1 → b.structural = .core 1 →
      a.marker = .boundary → b.marker = .idle → Unary a b
  | enter (a b : Cell) :
      a.structural = .stop → b.structural = .stop →
      a.marker = .boundary → b.marker = .full → Unary a b
  | unenter (a b : Cell) :
      a.structural = .stop → b.structural = .stop →
      a.marker = .full → b.marker = .boundary → Unary a b
  | control (a b : Cell) :
      a.marker = .full → b.marker = .full → Unary a b

inductive Rule : List Cell → List Cell → Prop where
  | unary {a b} : Unary a b → Rule [a] [b]
  | wider {u v} : 2 ≤ u.length → u.length = v.length → Rule u v

def Step (u v : List Cell) : Prop :=
  ∃ pre post lhs rhs,
    u = pre ++ lhs ++ post ∧
    v = pre ++ rhs ++ post ∧ Rule lhs rhs

inductive Trace : List Cell → List Cell → Prop where
  | refl (u) : Trace u u
  | tail {u v w} : Trace u v → Step v w → Trace u w

inductive UnaryZero : Cell → Prop where
  | format (a) : a.formatOK = false → UnaryZero a
  | firstRight (a) : a.marker = .right → UnaryZero a
  | lastLeft (a) : a.marker = .left → UnaryZero a
  | full (a) : a.marker = .full → UnaryZero a
  | checker (a n) :
      a.structural = .palette n → a.checkerIdle = false → UnaryZero a

inductive DeclaredZero : List Cell → Prop where
  | unary {a} : UnaryZero a → DeclaredZero [a]
  | wider {u} : 2 ≤ u.length → DeclaredZero u

def ContainsZero (u : List Cell) : Prop :=
  ∃ pre post factor, u = pre ++ factor ++ post ∧ DeclaredZero factor

def Nonzero (u : List Cell) : Prop :=
  ∀ v, Trace u v → ¬ ContainsZero v

def Released (u : List Cell) : Prop :=
  ∀ a ∈ u, a.marker = .idle

def CanRelease (u : List Cell) : Prop :=
  ∃ v, Trace u v ∧ Released v

theorem no_unary (p : Nat) (hp : p ≠ 1) (b : Cell) :
    ¬ Unary (cursor p) b := by
  intro h
  cases h with
  | create a b hs _ hm _ =>
      simp [cursor] at hm
  | uncreate a b hs _ _ _ =>
      simp [cursor] at hs
      exact hp hs
  | enter a b hs _ _ _ =>
      simp [cursor] at hs
  | unenter a b _ _ hm _ =>
      simp [cursor] at hm
  | control a b hm _ =>
      simp [cursor] at hm

theorem no_unary_zero (p : Nat) : ¬ UnaryZero (cursor p) := by
  intro h
  cases h <;> simp_all [cursor]

theorem no_step (p : Nat) (hp : p ≠ 1) (v : List Cell) :
    ¬ Step [cursor p] v := by
  rintro ⟨pre, post, lhs, rhs, hu, _, hr⟩
  have hlen : 1 = pre.length + lhs.length + post.length := by
    simpa using congrArg List.length hu
  cases hr with
  | @unary a b hab =>
      have hpre : pre = [] := by
        apply List.length_eq_zero.mp
        simp only [List.length_singleton] at hlen
        omega
      have hpost : post = [] := by
        apply List.length_eq_zero.mp
        simp only [List.length_singleton] at hlen
        omega
      subst pre
      subst post
      simp only [List.nil_append, List.append_nil, List.cons.injEq,
        and_true] at hu
      subst a
      exact no_unary p hp b hab
  | wider htwo _ =>
      omega

theorem trace_fixed (p : Nat) (hp : p ≠ 1) {v : List Cell}
    (h : Trace [cursor p] v) : v = [cursor p] := by
  generalize heq : [cursor p] = u at h
  induction h with
  | refl u => exact heq.symm
  | @tail u v w h hstep ih =>
      have hv : v = [cursor p] := ih heq
      subst v
      exact False.elim (no_step p hp w hstep)

theorem no_contains_zero (p : Nat) : ¬ ContainsZero [cursor p] := by
  rintro ⟨pre, post, factor, hu, hz⟩
  have hlen : 1 = pre.length + factor.length + post.length := by
    simpa using congrArg List.length hu
  cases hz with
  | @unary a ha =>
      have hpre : pre = [] := by
        apply List.length_eq_zero.mp
        simp only [List.length_singleton] at hlen
        omega
      have hpost : post = [] := by
        apply List.length_eq_zero.mp
        simp only [List.length_singleton] at hlen
        omega
      subst pre
      subst post
      simp only [List.nil_append, List.append_nil, List.cons.injEq,
        and_true] at hu
      subst a
      exact no_unary_zero p ha
  | wider htwo =>
      omega

theorem cursor_nonzero (p : Nat) (hp : p ≠ 1) : Nonzero [cursor p] := by
  intro v hv
  rw [trace_fixed p hp hv]
  exact no_contains_zero p

theorem cursor_not_releasable (p : Nat) (hp : p ≠ 1) :
    ¬ CanRelease [cursor p] := by
  rintro ⟨v, hv, hrelease⟩
  rw [trace_fixed p hp hv] at hrelease
  have hmark := hrelease (cursor p) (by simp)
  simp [cursor] at hmark

theorem parameter_uniform_counterexample
    (q p : Nat) (_hq : 3 ≤ q) (hp : 1 < p) (hpq : p < q) :
    1 ≤ p ∧ p ≤ q ∧
      Nonzero [cursor p] ∧ ¬ CanRelease [cursor p] := by
  have hp1 : p ≠ 1 := by omega
  exact ⟨by omega, by omega, cursor_nonzero p hp1,
    cursor_not_releasable p hp1⟩

theorem chosen_position (q : Nat) (hq : 3 ≤ q) :
    Nonzero [cursor 2] ∧ ¬ CanRelease [cursor 2] := by
  have h := parameter_uniform_counterexample q 2 hq (by omega) (by omega)
  exact h.2.2

end FiniteRuleBoundary

claims.natural_statement: At a legal large parameter, every actual unary replacement incident on a boundary cursor is either creation/inverse creation at C(1), or boundary/full conversion at S; all other actual unary controls have marker F on both sides. The displayed B at C(2) satisfies every unary format and no unary zero.

Over every field and every legal sufficiently large hierarchy parameter, mapping the displayed B at C(2) to [[0,1],[0,0]] and all other letters to zero defines a representation of A_h in 2-by-2 matrices and makes this singleton word nonzero.

For every legal sufficiently large parameter, the one-letter word B at C(2) with l=b=1, task rep, side zero, both data slots and certificate zero is a locally admissible nonzero truncated L*B region with no replacement successor and no release. It refutes the unqualified boundary-cursor sentence of fr:rollback if that sentence includes the explicitly permitted truncated word-end regions.

Lemma fr:palette-soundness: a complete initially checker-idle palette with each color once cannot reach a palette zero under arbitrary transaction interleavings; a complete palette in a nonzero word permits checker removal and, after transaction release, has every color once and sorts canonically.

Lemma fr:fragment-bound: every palette fragment in a nonzero word has length at most 16q+2; every cut-free interval has bounded length depending only on h, including intervals meeting either word end.

Every locally admissible interval between consecutive cuts has one to k complete structural blocks and either one complete transaction (possibly a partially acquired prefix beginning at its known first position) or one idle block; no truncated missing-left-endpoint transaction can occur in such an interval.

September cancellation.tex, ca:all-tests and thm:algebra: the hierarchy and cancellation reductions yield an infinite finitely presented graded algebra over F_2 whose positive-degree ideal is matrix-nil in every fixed finite dimension.
September thm:main: the constructed St_12(R) is infinite, ordinarily finitely presented, and periodic; besides the matrix-nil algebra this requires finite presentation and Steinberg-kernel torsion.

In the explicitly enlarged projection of the unary-source and zero schemas in Main.lean, for all natural q>=3 and 1<p<q, a format-valid singleton B cursor at C(p) is nonzero and cannot reach an all-idle word.

claims.natural_statement: September cancellation.tex: the actual direct-cancellation, token/chunk, automaton and dimension-growth arguments prove ca:all-tests and matrix nilpotence once the hierarchy is supplied.
The finite algebra presentation yields an ordinary finite presentation of St_12(R), without imposing extra group identities.
The kernel J_12(R) of St_12(R) to E_12(R) is torsion; periodicity of the elementary image alone does not establish this.
The infinite constructed ring gives infinitely many distinct elementary matrices and therefore infinitely many elements of St_12(R).
